title: Athena End To End Ai Agent
shortDescription: Production-Ready TTS Microservice (Supertonic ONNX) Architecture • Folder Structure • Deployment • Scaling • APIs • Best Practices Fully tuned for AI agent usage. What This Serv...
description: **Athena** is a desktop‑bound, autonomous 3D AI companion that blends real‑time **Three.js** rendering of VRM avatars with a local AI microservice stack. Built on an **Electron** host that bridges a Vite‑powered React UI to Python and Node services via IPC, it delivers *zero‑latency* speech‑to‑text using **Whisper‑fast**, high‑fidelity text‑to‑speech via **SuperTonic**, and intelligent behavior orchestrated by **LangGraph** agents. The stack leverages `@athena-ai/core` adapters for multiple TTS/STT providers, enabling seamless fallback to browser APIs.
longDescription:
The system is organized into three primary layers. The **Presentation Layer** consists of a React/Vite front‑end that hosts the `<AthenaWidget />` component, rendering the avatar with a custom Three.js pipeline, MediaPipe‑driven face tracking, and lip‑sync driven by FFT audio analysis. The **Inter‑Process Communication Layer** uses Electron’s `contextBridge` and async IPC channels to relay user interactions, audio streams, and control commands between the renderer and the **Main Process**, which manages window lifecycles and spawns local microservices. *Security guardrails* include isolated preload scripts, strict content‑security policies, and validation of inbound messages before they reach the AI engine.

The **Local Microservice Layer** runs a Python FastAPI **Whisper‑fast** STT server (`POST /stt`, `GET /status`) and a Node.js **SuperTonic** TTS server (`POST /tts`, `GET /health`). These services expose minimal HTTP endpoints, avoiding external network calls and ensuring privacy. The **LangGraph** orchestrator (`LangGraph Agent`) consumes transcriptions, routes them through LLM providers (Google Gemini, Ollama, custom agents via `CustomAgentAdapter`), and returns responses that are spoken back through the TTS stack. The architecture diagram in the project details visualizes these interactions as a directed graph of UI, IPC, and microservice nodes.

Build topology is managed by a single `npm start` command that concurrently launches the Electron host, Vite dev server, and the Python/Node services, each binding to dynamically allocated ports to prevent collisions. The codebase is typed with **TypeScript**, linted via **ESLint**, and packaged for cross‑platform distribution using Electron’s build tools. All components are modular, allowing developers to swap adapters (e.g., `OpenAITTSAdapter`, `AzureTTSAdapter`, `WebSpeechSTTAdapter`) without altering core logic.
myContributions: Architected a modular microservice application using Electron IPC to bridge a Vite React frontend with local Python and Node services.
Developed a custom Three.js rendering pipeline for VRM and FBX models, achieving stable 60 FPS performance.
Implemented deep GPU memory management via `deepDispose` and enforced high‑performance WebGL contexts.
Integrated LangGraph for dynamic tool orchestration, enabling web search, weather, timer, and RAG capabilities.
Built a zero‑latency local voice stack combining Whisper‑fast (STT) and SuperTonic (TTS) with real‑time audio streaming.
Added MediaPipe‑based face and eye tracking to maintain avatar eye contact and natural blinking.
Created FFT‑driven lip‑sync mapping audio frequencies to blendshape weights, reducing CPU overhead.
Designed fallback adapters (`WebSpeechTTSAdapter`, `WebSpeechSTTAdapter`) for browser‑only environments.
Implemented robust event system in `AthenaEngine` for status changes, speech lifecycle, and error handling.
Established a unified `CustomAgentAdapter` allowing plug‑in of arbitrary LLM endpoints with custom request/response transforms.

features: Real‑time 3D avatar rendering with VRM and FBX support.
High‑fidelity text‑to‑speech using SuperTonic with optional cloud providers (OpenAI, Azure, ElevenLabs).
Dynamic tool execution through LangGraph agents (search, weather, timer, RAG).
MediaPipe face tracking for eye contact and blink animation.
FFT‑based lip‑sync that maps audio to facial blendshapes.
Electron IPC bridge that isolates UI from backend services.
Theme support (`dark`, `light`) and customizable avatar model URL.
Graceful fallback to browser Web Speech API when no API keys are provided.
challenges: Balancing GPU memory usage while loading high‑poly VRM models required custom disposal logic.
Ensuring sub‑100 ms TTS latency demanded a native Node TTS engine and careful audio buffering.
Coordinating dynamic port allocation for STT/TTS services without collisions added complexity to the startup script.
Maintaining synchronization between IPC events and UI state under heavy AI load required debounced listeners.
Providing accurate lip‑sync without excessive CPU usage led to the adoption of FFT‑based mapping instead of full phoneme analysis.
learnings: Electron IPC can serve as a performant, secure bridge when combined with strict preload validation.
Local Whisper models deliver acceptable accuracy for desktop use while keeping user data private.
Modular adapter patterns simplify swapping between cloud and on‑device AI services.
FFT‑based lip‑sync offers a good trade‑off between realism and computational cost.
Dynamic service discovery (port negotiation) is essential for developer ergonomics in multi‑service desktop apps.
architectureOverview: Frontend built with React, TailwindCSS. Backend API powered by WebSockets, Express, FastAPI. AI/ML capabilities powered by ONNX Runtime. Deployed using Docker.

futureRoadmap: Add support for additional LLM backends via `CustomAgentAdapter` (e.g., Anthropic, Cohere).
Implement a plug‑in system for third‑party tools within the LangGraph orchestration layer.
Introduce persistent RAG memory using a lightweight vector store (e.g., SQLite + ONNX embeddings).
Provide a Docker Compose setup to simplify multi‑service deployment on non‑developer machines.
Enhance security by signing IPC messages and adding sandboxed renderer processes.

remotionVideoScript.voiceoverScript: Welcome to the technical breakdown of athena-end-to-end-ai-agent, a production-grade application engineered with TypeScript, JavaScript, Python. System Architecture & Topology: The application uses a decoupled multi-tier architecture powered by WebSockets, Express, FastAPI on the backend and React, TailwindCSS on the client. Network Routes: The API exposes 4 primary routes including GET /health and POST /tts and GET /status, managing request routing and data serialization. AI Capabilities: Powered by ONNX Runtime, delivering real-time inference and intelligent processing. Performance & Quality: Automated quality checks and clean component patterns ensure high reliability. Explore the full open-source codebase on GitHub at Sameer-Bagul slash athena-end-to-end-ai-agent.
